abstain_when: The request shifts from evidentiary analysis to obtaining, asserting, or substituting for production deployment authority; no research output may serve as an authority grant.
The artifact is shown not to be a verbatim reproduction of the delivery policy; report the premise failure instead of concluding on a different question.
No primary or official governance or evidence-standard source is accessible; do not close the corroboration determination on derivative or inaccessible sources alone.
mission.acceptable_uncertainty: A determination may state that verbatim mirrors are derivative and not independent corroboration only when supported by at least two independent authoritative sources; any residual uncertainty about the specific mirror's provenance, or a single-publisher evidence base, must be reported explicitly rather than resolved by assumption.
mission.audience: Enterprise governance, risk, and platform-engineering reviewers assessing deployment-governance evidence, and the requester deciding whether the mirror may be cited as corroboration.

clarifications.question: If sources indicate the mirrored text is not a verbatim reproduction of the authoritative delivery policy (e.g., independently authored or modified), should the mission pivot to that artifact's independence or close with a premise-unmet finding?
clarifications.trigger: Research reveals the mirrored text diverges from the authoritative delivery policy or has a separate authoring origin.

mission.decision: Determine whether a verbatim mirror repetition of the delivery policy constitutes independent corroboration of production deployment authority in the enterprise agentic software factory's deployment-governance evidence chain; the output is an evidentiary determination only and is not a grant, denial, or substitute for deployment authority.

freshness.rationale: Deployment-governance standards and policy status change over time; the corroboration determination must reflect the governance corpus as it currently stands, not a prior state.

obligations.closure_rule: Closed when criteria from at least two independent authoritative sources are captured and cited; if fewer are accessible, report the shortfall and leave the obligation open.
obligations.description: Locate primary or official governance and evidence-standard sources defining source independence; capture their criteria verbatim or by precise paraphrase.

obligations.closure_rule: Closed when provenance is established from accessible sources with the classification cited, or when no accessible source establishes provenance and the gap is reported as unresolved.
obligations.description: Establish, from available sources, the provenance of the mirror's delivery-policy text relative to the authoritative delivery policy; classify as derivative or separate-origin.

obligations.closure_rule: Closed when requirements are captured from primary or official sources with publisher count reported, or reported as not established within budget.
obligations.description: Capture the deployment-governance requirements for production deployment authority and the evidence those requirements demand.

obligations.closure_rule: Closed when the counterevidence search is executed and its results, including null results and any contradictions, are reported.
obligations.description: Search authoritative sources for any explicit treatment of verbatim mirrors or replicas as independent corroboration of deployment authority; preserve contradictions rather than resolving them.

obligations.closure_rule: Closed when context is captured or budget exhausts; this optional obligation is dropped first under budget pressure.
obligations.description: Capture governance-source statements on permitted roles of mirrors or replicas to distinguish legitimate uses from evidentiary corroboration.

questions.text: Under recognized governance and evidence standards, what criteria determine whether a source is independent, and does a verbatim reproduction of a policy document meet them?

Do available primary or official sources establish whether the mirror's delivery-policy text shares provenance with the authoritative delivery policy (derivative) or originates from a separate authoritative act?
How do accessible governance sources define production deployment authority, and what evidence do they require to establish it?

Is there any authoritative source that explicitly treats verbatim duplication or mirroring as independent corroboration of deployment authority? Preserve any contradiction with the derivativeness analysis.
What role, if any, do governance sources assign to mirrors or replicas (e.g., availability, redundancy, audit retention) distinct from evidentiary corroboration?

exclude: Any determination that production deployment authority exists, is granted, or is sufficient; the mission yields evidentiary analysis only, never an authority grant or permission.
Execution, configuration, or approval of any production deployment, and any change to deployment enforcement mechanisms.
Non-verbatim restatements, re-approvals, or independently authored policies; the request concerns verbatim repetition only.
Security testing or attempts to bypass deployment controls beyond what governance sources state.
include: Evidentiary status of any artifact that reproduces the delivery policy verbatim (repository mirrors, document copies, mirrored agent or system outputs, mirrored configurations) with respect to production deployment authority.
Recognized enterprise governance, change-management, and software-factory control standards on what evidence establishes production deployment authority and what counts as independent corroboration.
Doctrinal treatment of derivative versus independent evidence: criteria for when a verbatim reproduction of a source can, or cannot, serve as a second independent source for the same facts.
Provenance of the mirror's delivery-policy text relative to the authoritative delivery policy: shared origin versus separate authoritative act.
The enterprise's own delivery and deployment governance definitions of production deployment authority and its required evidence, where accessible in primary or official sources.

stop_when: Independence criteria from at least two independent authoritative sources are captured and applied to verbatim reproduction, yielding a supported determination or an explicit unsupported finding.
The mirror's provenance relative to the authoritative delivery policy is established from sources, or reported as unestablishable within budget.
Budget limits (4 searches, 10 sources, 6 model calls, 300 seconds) are reached; report partial findings and open gaps.

result.rationale: The request poses a well-formed evidentiary question, so research is appropriate and no blocking clarification is required: the request's own wording ('repeats the delivery policy verbatim') fixes the object of study as a verbatim reproduction, making artifact-type ambiguity non-decision-changing, and the scope covers all verbatim-reproduction forms without guessing. The mission is a research boundary only — it neither grants nor denies production deployment authority, treats the mirror as evidence to be provenance-checked rather than as permission, and its abstain_when rules block any use of the output as an authority grant.
